summary: Sets out the requirements and assumptions for a 0-byte IP/UDP/RTP header compression scheme, including what the underlying link layers should provide. It guided work in the ROHC working group. It is informational.

eli5.summary: Before building a way to shrink packet labels to nothing, the builders wrote down what they needed and what they assumed. This is that list.

questions: rohc ip udp rtp compression assumptions
rohc ip udp rtp compression requirements
why compress rtp headers on cellular links
subtitle: The requirements and link assumptions for squeezing IP/UDP/RTP headers down to zero bytes.

tldr.problem: Even the one-octet header of ROHC RTP is costly on cellular links such as GSM and IS-95, where adding a single octet forces a jump to the next fixed packet size.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC sets requirements for a 0-byte IP/UDP/RTP compression scheme as differences from regular ROHC RTP, and assumes the lower layer supplies the sequencing and timing the header used to carry.
tldr.outcome: It guided the ROHC Working Group's work on such a scheme. The memo is informational and defines no protocol itself.

today: RFC 3243 is an Informational memo from April 2002, and the metadata shows no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. The RFC itself names the link-layer assisted profile in RFC 3242 as an example of a protocol meeting these requirements.

sections.title: Why Zero Bytes
sections.content:
The ROHC Working Group develops header compression that performs well over links with high error rates and long round-trip times, such as cellular links using WCDMA, EDGE and CDMA-2000. ROHC RTP can already compress IP/UDP/RTP headers down to a total of only one octet.

Existing air interfaces such as GSM and IS-95 use radio bearers tuned to specific frame sizes that match the speech codecs. On them, not a single octet of header can be added without switching to the next higher fixed packet size, which is very costly. 0-byte header compression aims to remove the header completely for most packets during normal operation, with the lost functions supplied by the lower layer.
sections.eli5: If a box only comes in fixed sizes, even one extra sticker can force you to use the next bigger box. Getting rid of the sticker completely avoids that.

sections.title: Assumptions About Use
sections.content:
0-byte compression is meant to make optimal use of certain links when the traffic pattern of a packet stream completely matches the characteristics of the link. The RFC does not assume that only matching streams will occur, but efficiency cannot be optimal otherwise.

It is assumed that lower layers can supply the functions that replace the 1-octet header. The example given is the synchronized nature of most cellular links, which can provide sequencing and timing information and make packet loss detection possible.
sections.eli5: The road itself keeps count and keeps time, so the packets do not need to carry their own numbers and clocks.

sections.title: Requirements as Deltas
sections.content:
The requirements are written as changes to those for regular ROHC RTP in RFC 3096. Compression has no new impact on Internet infrastructure, so the Transparency and Ubiquity requirements apply unchanged.

For supported headers, arbitrary RTP streams must still be handled, so the scheme may not assume particular RTP behavior. Traffic that does not suit the link must make the scheme automatically and immediately fall back to non-0-byte RTP compression with no effect on the packet stream.

IPSEC is a special case. 0-byte compression cannot work if parts of the original headers are encrypted or carry randomly changing fields, so the scheme must fall back to a less efficient mode that handles every header field present.
sections.eli5: If a packet does not fit the shortcut, the system must instantly switch to the normal way without anyone noticing.

sections.title: Performance Requirements
sections.content:
All performance requirements of RFC 3096 still apply, with three changes.

  • Efficiency: for streams that match the link, 0-byte headers should be produced most of the time during normal operation, replacing most 1-octet headers. Spectrum efficiency is a primary goal.
  • Coexistence: the scheme must fit into the ROHC framework alongside other profiles and share as much as possible with the regular IP/UDP/RTP profile, to keep implementation simple.
  • Unidirectional links: working over them is of less importance, since 0-byte compression targets links that are typically bi-directional.
sections.eli5: The shortcut should be used almost all the time, should look like the normal method so it is easy to build, and is made for two-way roads.

sections.title: IANA and Security
sections.content: A protocol that meets these requirements, for example the link-layer assisted profile in RFC 3242, will need the IANA to assign various numbers and may have its own security aspects. This document by itself needs no IANA involvement and adds no security risks.
sections.eli5: This note is only a list of wishes, so it does not open any new doors for trouble. The actual tool built from it has to think about that.

cells: Zero bytes most of the time
